matter_reference_date_basis: Exam session APRIL 2020 as recorded in the candidate matter file. The operative events (Deed No. 234 of 23 March 2015, the death of Sunil Peiris on 6 December 2016 and the termination of Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T on 7 May 2018) all precede it.
corpus_gaps: Partition Law No. 21 of 1977 is not in the frozen corpus. It is the authority that makes a final decree in a partition action conclusive against the world and therefore the best root of title, which is the pivot of question M068-Q01.

The conveyancing standard of a good root of title (an instrument old enough, dealing with the whole legal and equitable interest, adequately describing the land and casting no doubt on the title) is not statutory in any enactment held in the corpus.

No enactment in the corpus governs road reservations created on a sub-division or the rights of the owners of Lots A, B and C in the reservation Lot R, so the nature of the undivided one-third share of Lot R could not be tested against statute.

Local authority and planning clearances that a purchaser would in practice also obtain (street line and building line certificates, non-vesting certificates, approved sub-division plans) sit in the Municipal Councils Ordinance, the Urban Councils Ordinance and the Urban Development Authority Law, but which authority covers Rajagiriya cannot be settled from the corpus, so no such provision was recorded for M068-Q03.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: The following sections of this Ordinance shall apply to the estates of such persons only as shall die after the proclamation of this Ordinance
provisions.why_relevant: Fixes the temporal scope of Part III. Sunil Peiris died in 2016, long after the proclamation, so the intestacy rules in sections 21 to 36 apply to his estate.
provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Inheritance ab interstate to the immovable property in Sri Lanka of a person deceased shall be governed and regulated by the following provisions of this Ordinance wherever such person may have or have had his actual or matrimonial domicile.
provisions.why_relevant: Lot B and the undivided one-third share of Lot R are immovable property in Sri Lanka, so devolution on Sunil Peiris's intestacy is governed by this Ordinance rather than by any other system of personal law.
provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: When any person shall die intestate as to any of his or her property, leaving a spouse surviving, the surviving spouse shall inherit one-half of the property of such person.
provisions.why_relevant: Gives the widow Kusum Peiris one-half of Sunil Peiris's estate, which is the first and largest step in the devolution of Lot B after his death.
provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Subject to the right of the surviving spouse in the preceding section mentioned, the right of inheritance is divided in the following order as respects (a) descendants, (b) ascendants, (c) collaterals.
provisions.why_relevant: Sets the order in which the remaining half devolves and confirms that the widow's half is taken off the top before descendants, ascendants and collaterals are considered.
provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants are preferent to all others in the estate of the parents; all the children take equally per capita
provisions.why_relevant: Establishes that descendants would exclude everyone else. Sunil Peiris died without children, so the descendant class fails and the next class must be reached.
provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: The children and remoter descendants failing, the inheritance of the deceased goes to his father and mother in case they are both alive; but if only one of the parents be alive, the surviving parent takes half, and the brothers and sisters of the deceased of the full blood, and the issue of any deceased brother or sister of the full blood, by representation, and the brothers and sisters of the half-blood who are related to the intestate by the side of the deceased parent, and the issue of any such deceased brother or sister of the half-blood, by representation, take the other half.
provisions.why_relevant: The operative rule. Sunil's father Charles Peiris predeceased him and his mother Pushpa Peiris survived, so Pushpa takes half of the remaining half and the full siblings together with the half-siblings related through the deceased father take the other half. It is also the provision that excludes Keerthi Perera, who is related only through the surviving parent.
provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: but if there are only half-brothers and sisters or such issue of one side, the full brothers and sisters and the issue of deceased full brothers and sisters by representation, take then in the first place one-half of the property, and divide the other half with the half-brothers and sisters and their issue by representation.
provisions.why_relevant: Governs how the collateral portion is split where the qualifying half-siblings are all on one side. Here only the paternal half-siblings Upul and Wimal qualify, so the full sisters Kanthi and Manel take one-half of the collateral portion first and share the balance with Upul and Wimal.
provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.
provisions.verifier_note: Excerpt and role confirmed against 15-1876/s27; the final limb was applied on the footing that section 25 admits only the paternal half-blood where the mother survives, so within the collateral half there are half-siblings of one side only. An alternative reading that divides the collateral half equally among all four siblings is arguable and would change the fractions; raised for the lawyer, not treated as a defect.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: if all those who succeed to the inheritance are equally near in degree to the intestate, they take per capita, and not per stirpes
provisions.why_relevant: Supplies the per capita basis on which the four surviving siblings divide the portion they share under section 27, all of them being in the same degree and all taking in their own right.
provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.

provisions.why_relevant: Explains why Deed of Transfer No. 234 of 23 March 2015 attested by a notary public is the form each link in the chain of title must take, and why every earlier and later link must likewise be a notarially attested instrument.
provisions.temporal_note: The corpus holds the consolidated text, which incorporates the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Acts No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024 (thumb impression and transferee execution requirements). At the date of Deed No. 234 (2015) and at 2020-04 section 2 required the writing to be signed by the party in the presence of a licensed notary and two or more witnesses and attested by them; the substance relied on, that a transfer of immovable property must be by a notarially attested deed, held then, the quoted words did not.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Every deed or other instrument, except any will, testament, or codicil required by this Ordinance to be executed or acknowledged before or to be attested by a notary, shall be executed, acknowledged, or attested in triplicate.

provisions.verifier_note: Temporal correction: triplicate is the word substituted by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 s.5. At 2020-04 section 16 read in duplicate. The background point (original, duplicate and protocol) survives, but the Q03 rule statement that deeds are executed in triplicate under s.16 is anachronistic for this matter.

provisions.why_relevant: Registration priority. It is why the devolution has to be traced through the Land Registry folios and why a search at the Colombo Land Registry is the step that tests whether the paper chain is also the registered chain.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: If the land consists of an undivided share in a land, the proportion which the share bears to the entire land shall be staled, and a description of the entire land shall be given as required by subsection (1).
provisions.why_relevant: Relevant to the description of Lot B as a divided allotment and of the one-third share of the road reservation Lot R as an undivided share, both of which must be described in the deed and traced separately.
provisions.temporal_note: Last amended in 1982, before the matter reference date.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: all duplicates and copies and all books and indexes kept under this Ordinance may be searched and examined by any person claiming to be interested therein or by his attorney-at-law or agent duly authorized thereto in writing, and certified copies of or extracts from any such duplicate, copy, or book may be obtained if required.

provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.

provisions.subsection: rule requiring a search of the land registry
provisions.relevant_excerpt: Before any deed or instrument (other than a will or codicil) affecting any interest in land or other immovable property is drawn by him, he shall search or cause to be searched the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title in regard to such land and whether any prior deed affecting any interest in such land has been registered
provisions.why_relevant: Puts the title search on a statutory footing as a duty of the notary who will draw the conveyance to the purchaser, and so identifies the search and its supporting documents as a necessary step before the sale is completed.

It does not govern the grant made by the District Court in Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T, so it does not support the proposition for which it was cited.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: No plan or map or copy or tracing of a plan or map shall be receivable in evidence in any court in Sri Lanka unless such plan or map has been prepared
provisions.why_relevant: Sets the condition a survey plan must satisfy to be usable as proof, and so supports requiring a plan certified by a registered licensed surveyor when Lot B and Lot R are identified on the ground against Plan No. 1125 and Partition Plan No. 567.
provisions.temporal_note: Section stands as originally enacted; the corpus records no amendment event, so the text was in force at the date of death (6 December 2016) and at the matter reference date 2020-04.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: unless grant of probate has been issued in the case of a person dying testate, or letters of administration or certificates of heirship have been issued in the case of a person dying intestate
provisions.why_relevant: Added by the verifier in place of the rejected section 554X. It is the provision that makes the testamentary-case documents legally necessary rather than merely useful: no transfer may be effected of property in the estate of a person who died within the five years before the transfer unless letters of administration or certificates of heirship have issued. Sunil Peiris died on 6 December 2016, so a conveyance at the matter reference date 2020-04 falls inside that window and the purchaser must see the grant made in District Court Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: if the present Ordinance is silent, the rules of the Roman-Dutch law as it prevailed in North Holland are to govern and be followed

It is the provision that makes Roman-Dutch law residual only, and so the provision on which the statute_only classification of Q02 depends: the Ordinance is not silent on any step of this distribution, so the enquiry never leaves the statute.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The devolution after Sunil Peiris's death is purely statutory and follows from the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance. The first half of the answer is not. What makes a final decree in a partition action a good root of title, and what a conveyancer means by a good root of title at all, rests on the Partition Law and on conveyancing practice and judicial authority; the Partition Law is not in the corpus and the good root of title standard is not statutory in any of the enactments that are.

legal_issues.issue: What document in the chain relating to Lot B is a good root of title, and why the final decree in District Court of Colombo Partition Case No. 1256/P is the natural starting point.
How title passed from Alfred Almeida to Sunil Peiris in respect of Lot B and the undivided one-third share of Lot R by Deed of Transfer No. 234 of 23 March 2015.
How Sunil Peiris's interest devolved on his intestate death on 6 December 2016 and who now stands on the pedigree.
Whether each link in the pedigree is supported by a registered instrument or by a court record.

questions.hop_count_basis: Root of title in the partition decree, then the notarial transfer, then the registration of that transfer, then the statutory intestate devolution through sections 21, 22, 25 and 27 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance. Only the last chain is fully supported inside the corpus.

enrichment.original_background: Anura Perera your client wants to purchase a house and property situated in Rajagiriya said to be belonging to one Kusum Peiris and gives you a copy of a Transfer Deed No. 234 dated 23rd March, 2015 attested by Walter de Silva Notary Public and a copy of a Survey Plan No.1125 dated 2nd January, 2000 made by Anil Silva Licensed Surveyor relating to an allotment of land marked Lot B together with a Reservation for a Road marked Lot R of the Land called Dewatagahawatta in extent of 30 perches situated in Rajagiriya. On examining the documents tendered and after a search at the Colombo Land Registry you observe that Lot B and R depicted in the said Survey Plan are sub-divisions of Lot 1 containing in extent of One Rood and 10 Perches depicted in Partition Plan No. 567 dated 4th April 1998 also made by Anil Silva Licensed Surveyor (herein after referred to as the Original land). 1. The Original Land was allotted to one Alfred Almeida by Final Decree in the District Court of Colombo Partition case No. 1256/P and subsequently by Survey Plan 1125 made by Anil Silva Licensed surveyor sub-divided the said Lot 1 into 4 allotments of land marked A,B,C.and R. and by Deed of Transfer No. 234 dated 23rd March 2015 attested by Walter de Silva Notary Public sold Lot B together with undivided 1/3rd share of the Road Reservation marked Lot R to Sunil Peiris. 2. Sunil Peiris had died Intestate without children on 6th December 2016 leaving behind his widow Kusum Peiris. His estate was duly Administered in District Court Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T and proceedings terminated on 7th May 2018.On examining the Testamentary Case it was observed that the father of Sunil Peiris one Charles Peiris had pre-deceased him leaving behind 2 children named Upul and Wimal by his 1st marriage to Kamala Peiris and three children named Sunil, Kanthi and Manel by his 2nd marriage to Pushpa Peiris. Pushpa Peiris was alive and she too had a child by her 1st marriage to Lal Perera named Keerthi Perera and three children named Sunil, Kanthi and Manel by her 2nd marriage to Charles Peiris.

gold_answer_draft.issue: The pedigree of Lot B has to be drawn from a good root of title, which means starting at the final decree in District Court of Colombo Partition Case No. 1256/P and tracing every subsequent link down to the persons who own Lot B today.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Once the root is fixed, each link must be a notarially attested instrument or a court record, and each instrument must be registered if it is to hold against a later registered instrument taken for value (Registration of Documents Ordinance s.7; Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2). Where a link is a death, devolution is statutory: inheritance to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance (s.21), the surviving spouse takes one-half (s.22), and on failure of descendants with only one parent surviving the surviving parent takes half of the balance while the full siblings and the half-siblings related through the deceased parent take the other half (s.25), divided as s.27 directs.
gold_answer_draft.application: Root: the final decree in District Court of Colombo Partition Case No. 1256/P allotted Lot 1, one rood and ten perches in Partition Plan No. 567 dated 4 April 1998, to Alfred Almeida. Alfred Almeida then sub-divided Lot 1 by Survey Plan No. 1125 dated 2 January 2000 into Lots A, B, C and the road reservation Lot R. By Deed of Transfer No. 234 dated 23 March 2015 attested by Walter de Silva, Notary Public, Alfred Almeida transferred Lot B together with an undivided one-third share of Lot R to Sunil Peiris. Sunil Peiris died intestate on 6 December 2016 without children, leaving his widow Kusum Peiris; his estate was administered in District Court Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T, which terminated on 7 May 2018. On that intestacy Kusum Peiris took one-half; his surviving mother Pushpa Peiris took one-fourth; his full sisters Kanthi and Manel and his paternal half-brothers Upul and Wimal took the remaining one-fourth between them; and Keerthi Perera, being related to Sunil only through the surviving mother, took nothing.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The pedigree runs: final decree in Partition Case No. 1256/P to Alfred Almeida, then Deed of Transfer No. 234 of 2015 to Sunil Peiris, then on his intestacy in 2016 to Kusum Peiris, Pushpa Peiris, Kanthi, Manel, Upul and Wimal. Kusum Peiris is therefore not the sole owner of Lot B. This answer is not complete on the corpus alone: the Partition Law, which is what makes the final decree conclusive and therefore a good root of title, is not in the frozen corpus, so the root of title limb of the answer is unsupported here.

answer_claims.claim_text: Inheritance ab intestato to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance.
A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the property of a person who dies intestate.

Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, the surviving parent takes half of the remainder and the full siblings together with the half-siblings related through the deceased parent take the other half, divided as section 27 directs.
An unregistered instrument is void against a later instrument duly registered and taken for valuable consideration, so every link in the pedigree must be traced through the Land Registry folios.
By Deed of Transfer No. 234 dated 23 March 2015 attested by Walter de Silva, Notary Public, Alfred Almeida transferred Lot B together with an undivided one-third share of Lot R to Sunil Peiris.

On Sunil Peiris's intestate death on 6 December 2016 without children, Lot B and the undivided one-third share of Lot R devolved on his widow Kusum Peiris, his surviving mother Pushpa Peiris, his full sisters Kanthi and Manel and his paternal half-brothers Upul and Wimal, to the exclusion of Keerthi Perera.
Kusum Peiris is not the sole owner of Lot B and cannot alone convey the whole of it to the purchaser.
The proposition that the final decree in the partition action is a good root of title cannot be supported from the frozen corpus, which does not contain the Partition Law.

questions.block_reason: The question asks for the pedigree to be drawn from a good root of title. The root here is the final decree in District Court of Colombo Partition Case No. 1256/P, and the authority that makes a partition final decree conclusive and therefore a good root is the Partition Law No. 21 of 1977, which is not in the frozen corpus. The good root of title standard itself is conveyancing practice and judicial authority, not statute. The devolution limb of the answer is fully supported by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance and is recorded above, but the question as a whole cannot be answered from statute in the corpus alone. Verification adds two points. First, PROV-M068-019 (Civil Procedure Code s.554X) was removed from the supporting set as a foreign-probate provision that does not apply to a Sri Lankan grant. Second, the nearest thing the corpus holds to conclusiveness of a decree is Civil Procedure Code s.207, which makes matters decided res adjudicata between the same parties only; it does not make a partition decree conclusive against the world, so it does not close the gap and was deliberately not added as a provision.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: Every step in the calculation is supplied by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance: the widow's half under section 22, the failure of descendants under sections 23 and 24, the split between the surviving parent and the qualifying collaterals under section 25, the division between full and one-sided half-siblings under section 27, and the per capita rule in section 30. No judicial authority or Roman-Dutch doctrine is needed, because section 36 sends the enquiry to Roman-Dutch law only where the Ordinance is silent, and it is not silent on any step here.

legal_issues.issue: What share the widow Kusum Peiris takes in Lot B and in the undivided one-third share of Lot R.
How the remaining half devolves where the intestate left no descendants, a surviving mother and a predeceased father.
Which half-siblings qualify, and in particular whether Keerthi Perera, related only through the surviving mother, takes anything.
How the collateral portion is divided between the full sisters and the paternal half-brothers.

questions.hop_count_basis: Four indispensable linked steps: section 21 fixes the governing law, section 22 takes the widow's half, section 25 splits the balance between the surviving parent and the qualifying collaterals, and section 27 divides the collateral portion between full and one-sided half-siblings.

The Original Land was allotted to one Alfred Almeida by Final Decree in the District Court of Colombo Partition case No. 1256/P and subsequently by Survey Plan 1125 made by Anil Silva Licensed surveyor sub-divided the said Lot 1 into 4 allotments of land marked A,B,C.and R. and by Deed of Transfer No. 234 dated 23rd March 2015 attested by Walter de Silva Notary Public sold Lot B together with undivided 1/3rd share of the Road Reservation marked Lot R to Sunil Peiris. 2. Pushpa Peiris was alive and she too had a child by her 1st marriage to Lal Perera named Keerthi Perera and three children named Sunil, Kanthi and Manel by her 2nd marriage to Charles Peiris.

gold_answer_draft.issue: What share of Lot B, and of the undivided one-third share of the road reservation Lot R, does each surviving heir of Sunil Peiris hold, he having died intestate and childless on 6 December 2016 leaving a widow, a surviving mother, two full sisters, two paternal half-brothers and one maternal half-brother?
gold_answer_draft.rule: Inheritance ab intestato to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance (s.21). The surviving spouse inherits one-half of the intestate's property (s.22), and subject to that right inheritance passes in the order descendants, ascendants, collaterals (s.23), descendants being preferent to all others (s.24). Where children and remoter descendants fail and only one parent is alive, the surviving parent takes half and the full brothers and sisters of the deceased, together with the half-brothers and sisters related to the intestate by the side of the deceased parent, take the other half (s.25). Where the qualifying half-siblings are all of one side, the full siblings first take one-half of that portion and divide the remaining half with the half-siblings (s.27), those equally near in degree taking per capita (s.30).
gold_answer_draft.application: Sunil Peiris died intestate on 6 December 2016 leaving no children, so the descendant class fails. His widow Kusum Peiris takes one-half of Lot B and of the undivided one-third share of Lot R under s.22. His father Charles Peiris had predeceased him and his mother Pushpa Peiris was alive, so under s.25 Pushpa takes half of the remaining half, that is one-fourth. The other one-fourth goes to the full sisters Kanthi and Manel, both children of Charles and Pushpa, together with Upul and Wimal, who are half-brothers related to Sunil by the side of the deceased parent Charles. Keerthi Perera is the child of Pushpa by her earlier marriage to Lal Perera and is therefore related to Sunil only through the surviving parent, so s.25 does not admit him. Because the qualifying half-siblings are all on the father's side, s.27 gives Kanthi and Manel one-half of that one-fourth, that is one-eighth or one-sixteenth each, and the remaining one-eighth is divided per capita under s.30 among Kanthi, Manel, Upul and Wimal, that is one thirty-second each.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The present heirs hold Lot B, and the undivided one-third share of Lot R, as follows: Kusum Peiris, the widow, one-half; Pushpa Peiris, the mother, one-fourth; Kanthi three thirty-seconds; Manel three thirty-seconds; Upul one thirty-second; Wimal one thirty-second. Keerthi Perera takes no share. The six shares exhaust the whole, so all six must join in any conveyance of the entirety of Lot B to the purchaser.

answer_claims.claim_text: Inheritance ab intestato to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, whatever the deceased's domicile.
A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the property of a person dying intestate.
Subject to the surviving spouse's half, inheritance devolves in the order descendants, ascendants, collaterals, descendants being preferent to all others.
Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, the surviving parent takes half and the full siblings together with the half-siblings related through the deceased parent take the other half.
Half-siblings related to the intestate only through the surviving parent are not admitted to the collateral half under section 25.

Where the qualifying half-siblings are all of one side, the full siblings take one-half of the collateral portion in the first place and divide the other half with the half-siblings, those equally near in degree taking per capita.
Sunil Peiris left no children, so the descendant class fails and his widow Kusum Peiris takes one-half of Lot B and of the undivided one-third share of Lot R.
Because Charles Peiris predeceased Sunil and Pushpa Peiris survived him, Pushpa takes one-fourth of the estate as the surviving parent.

Kanthi and Manel are Sunil's full sisters and Upul and Wimal are half-brothers by the side of the deceased father Charles, so those four share the remaining one-fourth, while Keerthi Perera, related only through the surviving mother, is excluded.
Applying section 27 to that one-fourth, Kanthi and Manel take one-eighth between them and the other one-eighth is divided per capita among Kanthi, Manel, Upul and Wimal.

The shares are Kusum Peiris one-half, Pushpa Peiris one-fourth, Kanthi three thirty-seconds, Manel three thirty-seconds, Upul one thirty-second and Wimal one thirty-second, and Keerthi Perera nothing.
All six heirs must join in a conveyance if the purchaser is to obtain the entirety of Lot B and of the undivided one-third share of Lot R.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: Each of the four classes of document named below has a statutory basis inside the corpus: certified folio extracts and certified copies of registered duplicates under sections 42 and 43 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, certified copies of court records under sections 205, 206, 531 and 554X of the Civil Procedure Code, notarially attested deeds and the notary's title search under section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance, and a plan certified by a registered licensed surveyor under section 13 of the Survey Act. The selection and ordering of the documents follows ordinary conveyancing practice, but no proposition asserted below depends on judicial authority.

legal_issues.issue: What documents evidence the registered state of the title to Lot B and the undivided one-third share of Lot R at the Colombo Land Registry.
What documents evidence each notarially attested link in the chain, including Deed of Transfer No. 234 of 2015.
What court records evidence the partition decree and the devolution of Sunil Peiris's interest on his heirs.
What survey documentation identifies Lot B and Lot R on the ground and ties Plan No. 1125 back to Partition Plan No. 567.

questions.hop_count_basis: Cross-enactment reasoning: the right to search and take certified extracts and the evidentiary value of those extracts under the Registration of Documents Ordinance, then the court records that prove the decree and the heirs under the Civil Procedure Code, then the survey plan that must be certified by a registered licensed surveyor under the Survey Act.

enrichment.original_background: Anura Perera your client wants to purchase a house and property situated in Rajagiriya said to be belonging to one Kusum Peiris and gives you a copy of a Transfer Deed No. 234 dated 23rd March, 2015 attested by Walter de Silva Notary Public and a copy of a Survey Plan No.1125 dated 2nd January, 2000 made by Anil Silva Licensed Surveyor relating to an allotment of land marked Lot B together with a Reservation for a Road marked Lot R of the Land called Dewatagahawatta in extent of 30 perches situated in Rajagiriya. On examining the documents tendered and after a search at the Colombo Land Registry you observe that Lot B and R depicted in the said Survey Plan are sub-divisions of Lot 1 containing in extent of One Rood and 10 Perches depicted in Partition Plan No. 567 dated 4th April 1998 also made by Anil Silva Licensed Surveyor (herein after referred to as the Original land). 1. The Original Land was allotted to one Alfred Almeida by Final Decree in the District Court of Colombo Partition case No. 1256/P and subsequently by Survey Plan 1125 made by Anil Silva Licensed surveyor sub-divided the said Lot 1 into 4 allotments of land marked A,B,C.and R. and by Deed of Transfer No. 234 dated 23rd March 2015 attested by Walter de Silva Notary Public sold Lot B together with undivided 1/3rd share of the Road Reservation marked Lot R to Sunil Peiris. 2. Sunil Peiris had died Intestate without children on 6th December 2016 leaving behind his widow Kusum Peiris. His estate was duly Administered in District Court Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T and proceedings terminated on 7th May 2018.On examining the Testamentary Case it was observed that the father of Sunil Peiris one Charles Peiris had pre-deceased him leaving behind 2 children named Upul and Wimal by his 1st marriage to Kamala Peiris and three children named Sunil, Kanthi and Manel by his 2nd marriage to Pushpa Peiris. Pushpa Peiris was alive and she too had a child by her 1st marriage to Lal Perera named Keerthi Perera and three children named Sunil, Kanthi and Manel by her 2nd marriage to Charles Peiris.

gold_answer_draft.issue: Which four classes of documentation should the purchaser Anura Perera obtain from the present owners and from the Land Registry in order to establish a clear chain of title to Lot B, together with the undivided one-third share of the road reservation Lot R?
gold_answer_draft.rule: Duplicates, copies, books and indexes kept under the Registration of Documents Ordinance may be searched by an interested person or his attorney-at-law, and certified copies of or extracts from them may be obtained (Registration of Documents Ordinance s.42); such a certified copy or extract is admissible without proof of the Registrar's signature and is prima facie evidence of the contents of the folio (s.43). Registration matters, because an unregistered instrument is void against a later duly registered instrument taken for value (s.7), and an instrument must describe a divided allotment by its own boundaries and an undivided share by the proportion it bears to the whole (s.13). Every transfer of immovable property must be by a notarially attested deed (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2, executed in triplicate under s.16), and the notary who is to draw the purchaser's conveyance must himself search the land registry to ascertain the state of the title (Notaries Ordinance s.31). Where a link is a court record, the decree or a certified copy of it is the sole primary evidence of what the court decided (Civil Procedure Code s.206), certified copies of the judgment, decree or proceedings are obtainable from the Registrar of the court (s.205), a certificate of heirship is sufficient proof of the true heirs and of each heir's share on an intestacy (s.531), and a sealed duplicate or certified copy of letters of administration has the same effect as the original (s.554X). A plan is receivable in evidence only if prepared and certified as the Survey Act requires (s.13).
gold_answer_draft.application: First, certified extracts of the relevant Colombo Land Registry folios: the folio for the original land, Lot 1 in Partition Plan No. 567, and the folio opened for Lot B and Lot R after the sub-division, showing the ownership and every registered encumbrance, lis pendens, caveat, mortgage or seizure down to the date of the search. These come under s.42 and carry the evidentiary weight given by s.43, and they are what shows whether Deed No. 234 was duly registered and so protected by s.7. Second, certified copies of every notarially attested deed in the chain, taken either from the registered duplicate in the Land Registry under s.42 or from the attesting notary's protocol, beginning with Deed of Transfer No. 234 dated 23 March 2015 attested by Walter de Silva, Notary Public, and including any later deed by which an heir has dealt with a share; each must satisfy s.2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and must describe Lot B by its own boundaries and the share of Lot R as an undivided one-third under s.13 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance. Third, certified copies of the court records that carry the title over the two links that are not deeds: the final decree and the partition plan filed in District Court of Colombo Partition Case No. 1256/P, obtained under s.205 and constituting under s.206 the primary evidence of the allotment of Lot 1 to Alfred Almeida; and the order, the letters of administration or certificate of heirship and the final proceedings in District Court Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T, obtained under s.205 and s.554X, the certificate of heirship being sufficient proof under s.531 of who the heirs of Sunil Peiris are and what share each takes. Fourth, a current survey plan with a superimposition, prepared and certified by a registered licensed surveyor, identifying Lot B and Lot R on the ground and tying Survey Plan No. 1125 dated 2 January 2000 back to Lot 1 of Partition Plan No. 567; a plan not so certified would not be receivable in evidence under s.13 of the Survey Act, and it is this document that shows whether the thirty perches recited in the deed match what is on the ground.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The purchaser should obtain, first, certified extracts of the relevant Colombo Land Registry folios; second, certified copies of every notarially attested deed in the chain, starting with Deed of Transfer No. 234 of 2015; third, certified copies of the final decree and plan in Partition Case No. 1256/P and of the order, letters of administration or certificate of heirship and final proceedings in Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T; and fourth, a current plan and superimposition certified by a registered licensed surveyor. Taken together these establish the chain from the partition decree to the persons who now hold Lot B and disclose any registered encumbrance. Nothing short of all four will show that Kusum Peiris cannot convey the entirety by herself.

answer_claims.claim_text: An interested person or his attorney-at-law may search the duplicates, copies, books and indexes kept under the Registration of Documents Ordinance and obtain certified copies of or extracts from them.
A copy or extract certified under the hand of a Registrar is admissible without proof of his signature or appointment and is prima facie evidence of the contents of the folio.
An unregistered instrument is void against a later instrument duly registered and taken for valuable consideration, which is why the registered state of the folio has to be checked.

A transfer of immovable property is of no force in law unless made by a deed in writing signed by the executants and witnesses before a notary and attested by him, and such deeds are executed in triplicate.
A notary must search the land registry before drawing an instrument affecting an interest in land, to ascertain the state of the title and whether any prior deed has been registered.

A decree or a certified copy of it is the sole primary evidence of the decision of the court, and certified copies of the judgment, decree or proceedings may be obtained from the Registrar of the court.

A certificate of heirship is sufficient proof of the true heirs of the deceased and of the share each is entitled to receive on an intestacy, and a sealed duplicate or certified copy of letters of administration has the same effect as the original.

A plan is receivable in evidence only if it has been prepared and certified as the Survey Act requires, and an instrument must describe a divided allotment by its own boundaries and an undivided share by the proportion it bears to the whole.

The purchaser should obtain certified extracts of the Colombo Land Registry folios for the original land and for Lot B and Lot R, showing ownership and every registered encumbrance down to the date of the search.

The purchaser should obtain certified copies of every notarially attested deed in the chain, beginning with Deed of Transfer No. 234 dated 23 March 2015 attested by Walter de Silva, Notary Public, taken from the registered duplicate or from the notary's protocol.

The purchaser should obtain certified copies of the final decree and plan in District Court of Colombo Partition Case No. 1256/P and of the order, letters of administration or certificate of heirship and final proceedings in District Court Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T.

The purchaser should obtain a current survey plan and superimposition certified by a registered licensed surveyor, identifying Lot B and Lot R on the ground and tying Survey Plan No. 1125 back to Lot 1 of Partition Plan No. 567.
These four classes of document, taken together, establish the chain of title from the partition decree to the persons who now hold Lot B and disclose any registered encumbrance affecting it.

questions.block_reason: Downgraded from proposed_gold on verification. The gold answer's rule and application both rely on Civil Procedure Code s.554X for the proposition that a sealed duplicate or certified copy of letters of administration has the same effect as the original; s.554X belongs to the FOREIGN PROBATES chapter (ss.554U-554BB) and does not apply to the grant made in District Court Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T, so that provision was rejected and the claims resting on it marked rejected or disputed. The rule paragraph also states that notarial deeds are executed in triplicate under s.16 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance; triplicate is the wording substituted by Act No. 30 of 2022 and at the matter reference date 2020-04 the section read in duplicate. The same caution applies to Civil Procedure Code s.205, which the corpus holds only in the form substituted by Act No. 20 of 2023. Civil Procedure Code s.545 was added as PROV-M068-901 to carry the testamentary-case documentation that s.554X was wrongly used for, but the gold answer prose does not cite it and the verifier may not rewrite that prose. A lawyer should re-draft the third document class and the triplicate sentence before this question is used as gold.
